SIRA Certification Overview - Security Guard Requirements
Comprehensive overview of SIRA (Security Industry Regulatory Agency) certification requirements for security guards in the UAE.

About SIRA (Security Industry Regulatory Agency)

SIRA is the regulatory body overseeing the private security industry in Dubai, UAE. All security personnel operating in Dubai must comply with SIRA standards and regulations.

SIRA Grade System

  • Grade 1 - Security Guard: Entry-level position for basic security duties
  • Grade 2 - Senior Security Guard: Experienced guards with additional responsibilities
  • Grade 3 - Security Supervisor: Supervisory role managing teams and operations
  • Grade 4 - Security Manager: Senior management overseeing security operations

Certification Requirements

To obtain SIRA certification, guards must:

  1. Complete approved security training courses (minimum 40 hours for Grade 1)
  2. Pass SIRA written and practical examinations
  3. Undergo background verification and security clearance
  4. Obtain medical fitness certificate
  5. Register with SIRA and obtain security guard permit

Code of Conduct

All SIRA-certified guards must adhere to:

  • Professional appearance and behavior at all times
  • Respect for laws, regulations, and client policies
  • Confidentiality of sensitive information
  • Non-discrimination and cultural sensitivity
  • Zero tolerance for corruption or unethical behavior

Renewal Requirements

SIRA permits must be renewed every 2 years. Renewal requires:

  • Updated medical fitness certificate
  • Completion of refresher training (minimum 8 hours)
  • Clean disciplinary record
  • Payment of renewal fees
Important: Operating as a security guard without valid SIRA certification is illegal and may result in fines and deportation.
Standards for security guard uniforms and professional appearance as per SIRA regulations.

SIRA Uniform Standards

Approved Uniform Colors

SIRA-approved uniforms must be in the following colors only:

  • Black
  • Dark Navy Blue
  • Dark Grey

Note: Khaki, green, or camouflage patterns are strictly prohibited as they resemble police or military uniforms.

Mandatory Uniform Components

  1. SIRA Badge: Visible on left chest or shoulder (company logo on right)
  2. Name Tag: Clear identification with guard's name and company
  3. Company Logo: Properly positioned and authorized by SIRA
  4. Uniform Shirt/Jacket: Clean, pressed, and in good condition
  5. Uniform Trousers: Matching color, proper fit
  6. Black Safety Shoes: Polished, closed-toe, slip-resistant
  7. Belt: Black leather or synthetic, with standard buckle

Personal Grooming Standards

  • Hair: Neat, clean, and professional. Long hair must be tied back.
  • Facial Hair: Well-groomed mustache/beard permitted. No unkempt appearance.
  • Nails: Clean and trimmed
  • Personal Hygiene: Daily shower, deodorant, fresh breath
  • Jewelry: Minimal and professional (wedding ring, watch only)

Equipment Carriage

Authorized equipment must be carried in designated pouches/holders:

  • Flashlight (right side)
  • Radio (left side or chest)
  • Notebook and pen
  • Mobile device (if authorized)
Prohibited: Wearing uniforms that resemble police, military, or civil defense is a criminal offense under UAE Federal Law.
UAE Labor Law - Rights and Responsibilities for Security Guards
Key provisions of UAE Federal Labor Law relevant to security personnel.

UAE Labor Law - Key Provisions for Security Guards

Working Hours

  • Standard: Maximum 8 hours per day, 48 hours per week
  • Ramadan: Reduced to 6 hours per day for Muslims
  • Overtime: Must be compensated at 125% of hourly rate (150% for night shifts)
  • Rest Periods: Minimum 1-hour break after 5 consecutive hours

Leave Entitlements

  • Annual Leave: 30 days per year (after 1 year of service)
  • Sick Leave: 90 days per year (full pay for first 15 days, half pay for next 30 days)
  • Public Holidays: All UAE national and Islamic holidays (paid)

End of Service Benefits

Gratuity calculation based on years of service:

  • Less than 1 year: No gratuity
  • 1-5 years: 21 days basic salary per year
  • More than 5 years: 30 days basic salary per year

Guard Rights

  • Written employment contract in Arabic (translated copy acceptable)
  • Safe working environment and proper equipment
  • Medical insurance as per Dubai regulations
  • Salary payment by 10th of each month
  • Passport retention by employee (employer cannot hold passport)
Know Your Rights: Contact the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE) for any labor disputes or concerns.
